skill.name: batch-grill-me
skill.description: A relentless interview that asks every frontier question at once, round by round, to surface every hidden decision in a plan before you build it.
skill.summary: A relentless interview that asks every frontier question at once, round by round.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: This is a prompt-only skill consisting of a SKILL.md instruction file and an agents/openai.yaml interface manifest, with no executable code, scripts, network calls, filesystem writes, or environment access. Static analysis detected zero suspicious patterns and there were no findings to adjudicate. Semantic review found no prompt injection, data-exfiltration intent, or business-logic abuse: the instructions describe a benign question-and-answer interview workflow that defers all decisions to the user.

content.user_title: Interview Your Plan Round by Round
content.value_statement: Plans fail because hidden decisions go unasked until they become expensive to change. This skill runs a structured interview that surfaces every open question in dependency order, so you reach a shared understanding before any work begins.
actual_capabilities: Maps a plan as a decision tree where each choice branches into the decisions that depend on it.
Asks every currently answerable question in a single round, each numbered with a recommended answer.
Waits for user answers before moving to the next round, so no question is asked before its prerequisites are settled.
Recomputes the open question set after each round as newly settled decisions unblock further questions.
Dispatches sub-agents to look up facts from the environment rather than asking the user for information it can find itself.
Ends only when every branch has been visited and nothing is left silently assumed.
limitations: It gathers understanding but does not execute the plan; it waits for explicit user confirmation before acting.
Answer quality depends on the user replying to each round, so the process stalls if questions go unanswered.
It is a prompt-only workflow with no tools of its own beyond the host agent's abilities.
It must be invoked by the user because model-initiated invocation is disabled.

use_cases.title: Scope a new feature before coding
use_cases.description: A developer describes a rough feature idea and the skill interviews them round by round to expose data models, edge cases, and integration points that were left vague.

use_cases.title: Pin down product requirements
use_cases.description: A product manager uses the interview to convert a loose concept into a fully specified set of decisions before handing it to a team.

use_cases.title: Align on a technical design
use_cases.description: A tech lead runs the skill to walk a design tree with stakeholders, ensuring each architectural choice is settled in dependency order.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Grill me on my plan to build a personal task tracker. Ask me everything you need to know, one round at a time.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first-time user with a simple idea

prompt_templates.title: Interview with a stated goal
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to add email notifications to my app. Interview me round by round until we share an understanding of exactly what to build.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user scoping a specific feature

prompt_templates.title: Interview with environment lookups
prompt_templates.prompt: Grill me on refactoring this project's authentication flow. Where a question needs a fact from the codebase, look it up yourself instead of asking me.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user who wants facts sourced from the environment

prompt_templates.title: Interview a complex multi-branch design
prompt_templates.prompt: I am designing a multi-tenant billing system. Map the full decision tree, ask each round of answerable questions with your recommended answers, and continue until nothing is left assumed.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user with a large design space

output_examples.input: Grill me on my plan to build a personal task tracker.
output_examples.output: Round 1. 1) Who is the tracker for, just you or a team? Recommended: just you, to keep scope small. 2) Where should tasks live, a local file or a hosted database? Recommended: a local file for a personal tool. 3) Do you need reminders or due dates? Recommended: due dates only for now. Please answer these before I open the next round.

output_examples.input: The user answers that it is single-user, local storage, with due dates.
output_examples.output: Those answers settle storage and scope, which unblocks the next round. Round 2. 1) What file format for local storage? Recommended: a plain JSON file for easy editing. 2) How should overdue tasks be shown? Recommended: highlighted at the top of the list. 3) Do you want a command line or a simple interface? Recommended: command line first. Answer these and I will recompute what remains.

best_practices: Answer every numbered question in a round before expecting the next round, since later questions depend on your current answers.
Let the skill look up facts from your environment rather than answering environment questions yourself.
Wait for the interview to reach a shared understanding and confirm it before you ask the skill to act on the plan.
anti_patterns: Skipping questions or giving partial answers, which leaves branches of the plan silently assumed.
Asking the skill to start building before the interview is complete and confirmed.
Answering environment or lookup questions manually instead of letting the skill find those facts.

faq.question: What does this skill actually do?
faq.answer: It interviews you about a plan, asking every currently answerable question in a single round, then recomputes and asks the next round until nothing is left assumed.

faq.question: Why does it ask several questions at once?
faq.answer: It groups all questions whose prerequisites are already settled into one round, so you make related decisions together instead of one at a time.

faq.question: Does it make decisions for me?
faq.answer: No. It gives a recommended answer for each question, but every decision is yours. It waits for your confirmation before acting.

faq.question: Will it ask me for information it could find itself?
faq.answer: No. When a question needs a fact from your environment, it dispatches a sub-agent to look it up rather than asking you.

faq.question: When does the interview end?
faq.answer: It ends when every branch of the plan has been visited and no open questions remain, at which point it asks you to confirm the shared understanding.

faq.question: Do I need to invoke it manually?
faq.answer: Yes. Model-initiated invocation is disabled, so you start the skill yourself when you want to be interviewed.
